record.title: generatePdf Cloud Function appends the static robot token to a caller-chosen URL and loads it in headless Chromium
record.description: The generatePdf onRequest function (europe-west1) has no authentication code and uses cors({origin:true}). It takes ?url= from the query string with no scheme or host validation. It appends the hardcoded robotToken=<static value> (pdf.ts:27-30) and loads the result with Puppeteer page.goto (pdf.ts:49). An attacker who can reach the function can supply a URL on a host they control and receive the token in the request line. The same string is accepted by the Go API as the shared robot credential (auth.go:30 defines it and auth.go:468 matches it in userFromIDToken, returning DetermineRobotUser(admin id from the platform header)), so a leaked token yields robot/admin-level API access. The browser also fetches arbitrary URLs from inside the Cloud Functions network (SSRF, including the metadata server), and the rendered result is returned as a PDF to the caller. Source review found no URL allowlist, no caller check and no invoker restriction in pdf.ts, index.ts or firebase.json. The remaining unknown is deployment: whether the deployed function is publicly invokable. The firebase-functions v2 onRequest default is a public invoker, and the web client needs browser access, which points to public. That cannot be proven from source. The repo's own docs/shipit-core-connector-plan.md:371-381 describes the same issue as open. Secondary: the name parameter is interpolated unescaped into footerTemplate HTML (pdf.ts:95), giving HTML injection into the PDF footer, which is limited and low impact. Content-Disposition (pdf.ts:101-104) uses name unquoted, but Node rejects CR/LF in header values, so there is no header splitting; the effect is limited to filename and parameter manipulation.
record.claimed_root_cause: An unauthenticated, CORS-open HTTP function concatenates a hardcoded long-lived bearer secret onto an unvalidated user-supplied URL and navigates a headless browser to it, with no host allowlist or caller authentication.

trace.scope: generatePdf = onRequest({memory,timeoutSeconds,region}, ...) with cors({origin:true}) at line 5; no invoker option and no auth check
trace.description: Public HTTP entrypoint; any caller who can reach the function can invoke it.
url = request.query.url, attacker-controlled; the only validation is a non-empty check (lines 22-25).
Appends the hardcoded robotToken=<static token> as a query parameter to the attacker-supplied URL (lines 27-30).

trace.scope: generatePdf handler, page.goto(url) in Puppeteer launched with --no-sandbox (line 34)
trace.description: Headless Chromium requests the attacker-chosen URL including the token, sending it to the attacker host (or to internal addresses). The page is rendered to PDF (line 81) and returned to the caller.
The leaked value matches robotToken (auth.go:30) and maps to DetermineRobotUser(admin id from the platform header), so the exfiltrated token is a usable credential against the API.

evidence.description: url taken straight from the query string; only an emptiness check (22-25).
Hardcoded robot token literal appended to the URL (key name robotToken; value not reproduced here).
name interpolated unescaped into footerTemplate HTML.
generatePdf exported with no invoker/auth wrapper; setGlobalOptions sets only region.
No invoker, ingress or IAM configuration for the function.
Same static string defined as the Go API robotToken constant; accepted at line 468.
Internal doc states the function is unauthenticated and leaks the token to caller-supplied URLs, and that rotation is still pending.

blockers: Whether the deployed Cloud Run service behind generatePdf grants roles/run.invoker to allUsers (public) is not visible in source. firebase-functions v2 onRequest defaults to a public invoker, but IAM could have been changed out of band.
Whether the deployed robotToken value is still live (not rotated) and whether egress from the function is unrestricted is not visible in source.
Whether the Go API at the deployed ingress honours the platform header for robot callers so the token yields real admin access, which depends on deployment configuration.

validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed checks only, no live probe: (1) in GCP console or via 'gcloud run services get-iam-policy generatepdf --region europe-west1', check whether allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers holds roles/run.invoker, and review ingress settings; (2) confirm in Secret Manager or the deployment config whether the robot token has been rotated since the commit; (3) review Cloud Run logs for generatePdf requests whose url host is not a Nile market origin.
validation_plan.local: In the Firebase emulator (port 5001 per firebase.json), call generatePdf with url set to a local listener the owner controls and confirm the listener receives robotToken in its query string; confirm that name containing HTML renders in the footer and that CR/LF in name causes a header error.

separate_root_causes: Static robot bearer token (and potatoesSa token) hardcoded in source: backend/go/auth/auth.go:30, backend/functions/firebase/functions/src/pdf.ts:30, client/market/graphql.config.ts:13, backend/loadtests/locust_testing.py:10, client/ios/README.md:10. Compromise of the repo or any client leaks full robot credentials.
pdf.ts:95 name parameter is unescaped HTML in the Puppeteer footerTemplate (low-impact HTML injection into the generated PDF footer; no header injection because Node rejects CR/LF).
